name: Baked Salmon With Cream Sauce
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: butter, melted in hot water
ingredients.originalText: 4 tablespoonfuls of butter, melted in hot water

instructions.text: Butter a sheet of foolscap paper on both sides
Wrap the fish up in it, pinning the ends securely together
Pour six or seven spoonfuls of butter-and-water over it
Steam in a moderate oven from three-quarters of an hour to an hour
Lift the cover from time to time to baste and assure yourself that the paper is not burning
Meanwhile have ready in a saucepan a cup of cream
Dissolve a bit of soda a little larger than a pea in the cream
Heat this in a double boiler
Thicken with a heaping teaspoonful of cornflour
Add a tablespoonful of butter, pepper and salt to taste
Add a liberal pinch of minced parsley
When the fish is unwrapped and dished pour half slowly over it
Send the rest to table in a boat
If you have no cream use milk and add a beaten egg to the thickening

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Butter a sheet of foolscap paper on both sides
2. Wrap the fish up in it, pinning the ends securely together
3. Lay it in the baking-pan
4. Pour six or seven spoonfuls of butter-and-water over it
5. Turn another pan over all
6. Steam in a moderate oven from three-quarters of an hour to an hour
7. Lift the cover from time to time to baste and assure yourself that the paper is not burning
8. Meanwhile have ready in a saucepan a cup of cream
9. Dissolve a bit of soda a little larger than a pea in the cream
10. Heat this in a double boiler
11. Thicken with a heaping teaspoonful of cornflour
12. Add a tablespoonful of butter, pepper and salt to taste
13. Add a liberal pinch of minced parsley
14. When the fish is unwrapped and dished pour half slowly over it
15. Send the rest to table in a boat
16. If you have no cream use milk and add a beaten egg to the thickening
